subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: Help me understand what's worth analyzing in these incident tickets.

judge.implied_focus: The nature/profile of IT incidents — characterizing each ticket by what failed, how it manifested, its scope, and resolution/timing context, effectively decomposing incidents into analyzable failure dimensions.

per_column.name: affected_system
per_column.rationale: Identifies the technical component involved — a core facet of what an incident is about and a strong analytical predictor.

per_column.name: symptom_type
per_column.rationale: Characterizes the failure mode; a coherent facet describing how the incident manifests.

per_column.name: incident_scope
per_column.rationale: Captures blast radius (individual vs infrastructure-wide), a meaningful severity/impact facet.

per_column.name: is_open_unresolved
per_column.rationale: Resolution-state facet of the incident lifecycle; actionable for backlog analysis.

per_column.name: self_resolved
per_column.rationale: Resolution-path facet distinguishing auto/self-resolution from intervention.

per_column.name: recurrence_signal
per_column.rationale: Flags recurring incidents — a genuinely useful analytical dimension, though its extreme skew (472/28) raises reliability concerns.

per_column.name: opened_hour_of_day
per_column.rationale: Temporal context facet useful for staffing/pattern analysis; derivable from opened_at.

per_column.name: access_context
per_column.rationale: Remote vs on-premise context; relevant facet though largely 'unspecified' (378), limiting its value.

judge.rationale: The columns collectively centre on one coherent inferable focus: profiling incident tickets by their failure characteristics and lifecycle context. They span differentiated, non-redundant facets — what failed (affected_system), how (symptom_type), scale (incident_scope), resolution (is_open_unresolved, self_resolved), recurrence, and temporal/access context — rather than a scattered grab-bag or mechanical text metrics. This is a sound decomposition at a useful granularity and directly actionable (an analyst can pivot on affected_system × symptom_type × scope to find hotspots). Deductions: recurrence_signal and access_context show very skewed/mostly-unspecified distributions suggesting weak inference reliability, and self_resolved partly overlaps with is_open_unresolved, slightly diluting structural cleanliness.
